questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Finland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Finland article.

questions.proof: The capital of Finland is Helsinki; the second largest city is Tampere.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Finland?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Finland article.

questions.proof: Finnish and Swedish both are the official languages of Finland; the most spoken languages is Finnish, mother tongue of about 90% of the population.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Its neighbours are _____ to the west, Norway to the north, Russia to the east and Estonia to the south, beyond the sea called Gulf of Finland.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “neighbours”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Finland article.

questions.proof: Its neighbours are Sweden to the west, Norway to the north, Russia to the east and Estonia to the south, beyond the sea called Gulf of Finland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The official currency of the country is the euro (EUR); before _____ it was the markka, the Finnish mark (FIM).”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Finland article.

questions.proof: The official currency of the country is the euro (EUR); before 2002 it was the markka, the Finnish mark (FIM).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Finland became independent of Russia on 6 December _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Finland article.

questions.proof: Finland became independent of Russia on 6 December 1917.
